title: Desktop Result Package (Muse -> GPT)
description: Muse's verified report of a Desktop Commander action, carried by HeavenzFire Interchange v1. This package is the ONLY proof a desktop action happened. A request package alone proves nothing. The commander key appears nowhere in it. Screenshots are referenced by sha256 + byte size only — never image data.

request_id.description: Echoes the request package's request_id verbatim.

source_platform.description: Results are always produced by Muse, the side that ran the executor.

host.description: The host label from the request.

status.description: ok = commander/executor performed the action and returned success. denied = the authorization check failed BEFORE any commander contact (ledger provably unmoved). failed = the action was attempted and failed, including honest 501 no-backend responses, recorded with their exact name. unknown = the commander was unreachable or the outcome did not come back; re-check state before any retry.

performed.description: What was actually done, step by step, e.g. 'executor validated package', 'POST /exec via commander at 127.0.0.1:18077 (host label: vm)', or 'no commander contact (denied at authorization check)'.

stdout.description: exec/file_read output, truncated to the commander's 64 KB cap where applicable.

exit_code.description: Null when no process ran (status 501s, denials, renders) or the command timed out.

commander_response.description: The commander's JSON response for non-exec actions (status fields, render title/text, click/type confirmations), verbatim.

output.description: Null when nothing was executed (denied / validation failure).

artifacts.description: References only — screenshots are delivered to Zachary in chat and never committed by default. No image data is ever carried in a package.

ledger_head_hash.description: sha256 of the commander's exact last ledger line (no trailing newline) after the action, per the commander's hash-chain convention. Null when the commander was not contacted (denied) or its ledger was not readable from the executor host.

ledger_entries.description: Commander ledger entry count after the action. Null under the same conditions as ledger_head_hash.

message.description: The commander's exact error text where one exists (e.g. its 501 message naming the missing backend), quoted. If nothing answered, say exactly that — do not invent a message.
